extra.message: The host query parameter is concatenated into _os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). A caller possessing the required x-internal-token can inject shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary commands with the application process's privileges.

extra.message: The fragment query parameter becomes executable template source in Template("Result: " + fragment).render(). When Jinja2 is available, a caller with the required x-internal-token can execute attacker-controlled expressions in an unrestricted template environment, enabling server-side code execution. The result is also returned as unescaped HTML.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The packet_ref query parameter is joined to BASE_EXPORT_DIR and read without checking containment. A caller with the required x-internal-token can supply ../ segments or an absolute path to read text files outside the export directory, including application configuration and credentials accessible to the process.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The name query parameter controls the path passed to mkdir() and write_bytes(), while the request body controls file contents. No containment check prevents relative traversal or absolute paths. A caller with the required x-internal-token can create or overwrite arbitrary files writable by the application process.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The url query parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(), and response contents are returned to the caller. A caller with the required x-internal-token can access loopback, private-network or metadata endpoints. Unrestricted schemes also permit file:// URLs to disclose local file contents. The timeout and 2048-byte read limit do not restrict destinations.

Lease creation checks management permission for the unit, but only checks that the supplied tenant_id exists. A manager can create a draft lease linking an unrelated tenant to a managed unit. The tenant read/update authorization in routes/tenants.py:81-85 and 107-111 then accepts this new relationship, granting access to that tenant's private profile and permission to modify internal notes.

Managers can list every tenant and maintenance worker because the query filters only by role, without checking assigned properties. UserOut exposes names, email addresses and phone numbers. The detail endpoint repeats this omission at lines 76-77, allowing managers to retrieve unrelated users by ID despite the application's property-scoped access rules.

Inspection access accepts any lease whose unit_id matches, regardless of lease dates or status. Former tenants can therefore read tenant-visible inspections created for subsequent occupants of their old unit. The listing repeats this check at lines 52-53, and routes/documents.py:56-61 similarly permits downloading documents attached to those inspections.

The authorization check intended to require an active lease collects units from every lease without checking status or dates. A tenant with an expired, terminated or future draft lease can submit new maintenance requests for that unit, including after another tenant moves in, and trigger manager notifications and maintenance workflows.

InspectionOut includes follow_up_notes for every caller. The inspection list and detail routes return this model to tenants without removing the field. frontend/src/pages/InspectionDetail.jsx explicitly labels these notes internal and hides them behind isStaff(), but tenants can read them directly in API responses.

cwe: CWE-201: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data

extra.message: CSV rows are written without neutralizing spreadsheet formula prefixes. Tenant-controlled full_name reaches the rent-roll export at line 213, and tenant-controlled ticket title/category reach the maintenance export at line 241. CSV quoting does not stop spreadsheet formula interpretation, so malicious values beginning with '=' can execute formulas when a manager opens the report.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: The active password-reset endpoint prints the plaintext reset token and associated email to standard output without a development-mode guard. Anyone able to read captured application output can use an unexpired token at /api/auth/password-reset/complete to replace the victim's password. The token remains valid for two hours.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The operations tally endpoint logs the complete Authorization header and request body at warning level. Valid requests carrying bearer credentials or confidential payloads expose those values to application logs and log readers. Neither credentials nor sensitive body fields are redacted.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The count query parameter has no upper bound and directly controls allocation of a list of dictionaries inside an async handler. A caller with the required x-internal-token can submit a huge count in a small request, exhausting memory or blocking the event loop. The nonce endpoint at lines 111-114 similarly performs unbounded allocation and iteration using the supplied length.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The lane query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse without restricting it to local paths or trusted destinations. Requests authenticated with x-internal-token can produce redirects to arbitrary external sites, allowing an attacker-controlled return destination to redirect a client away from the trusted application.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Unauthenticated registration returns HTTP 409 when an email already exists and HTTP 201 when it does not. Supplying otherwise valid registration fields reveals whether a target email has an account despite the generic error text. Login also exposes account existence through its distinct locked-account response at lines 82-83.

SESSION_SECRET defaults to a publicly known constant and is accepted without validation. security.py:18 uses it to sign session cookies when no environment override exists, allowing anyone to generate valid signatures for known session IDs. Random server-side session IDs still prevent fabricating an unknown victim session, but the cookie-signature protection is compromised under the default configuration.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Session cookies are always created with secure=False, including when the application is accessed over HTTPS. Browsers may therefore send the authentication cookie over an HTTP connection to the same host, exposing a reusable session credential to network interception. No runtime setting enables the Secure attribute.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
